tonight.headline: The lineup is the projection lineup; Taylor and Downs are under way in London
body: Bad news first, and there's little of it. Ollie Gordon, the back you spent your priority on, sits on the bench again in a backfield Miami say they'll split, and the Ravens D/ST are without Trey Hendrickson. Nothing else went against you overnight. Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton are both inactive in London, so Josh Downs is the Colts' lead receiver, and Jalen Coker is unlikely to play tonight, which is the game Darren Waller's targets came in. ESPN has you at 124.2 against Team 13's 88.3, 69%.

Nothing to do. The lineup as set is the projection lineup and no starter carries a designation. It's before the inactive lists, so re-check each starter 90 minutes before his kickoff: 09:30 for Lawrence, Barkley, Wilson and the Ravens, 12:55 for Rice and Myers, 16:50 for Waller.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Team 13 still start DeVonta Smith and Rachaad White, both ruled out, at 0.0 each, with Kyle Pitts (7.4) at tight end. On their bench: Lamar Jackson 20.3, DJ Moore 13.0, Dalton Kincaid 10.7 and Blake Corum 8.1. Josh Allen has no designation.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 moving Moore and Corum in for Smith and White: about 21 projected points back, which takes 88.3 to roughly 109 and the game to something much closer.

whatWentWrong.title: The tight-end seat: four changes in ten days, and this one may have landed
whatWentWrong.lead: Hockenson, Gadsden, Sadiq, now Waller. Overnight the condition Waller's role depended on moved his way.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Waller: 2, 3, 8 targets (archive); the 8 came once Coker left in Week 3. Schefter reported this morning that Coker is unlikely to play, and ESPN lifted Waller from 9.3 to 10.1. Sadiq is still questionable and leans toward playing (SI, 4 Oct); he's on waivers until Wednesday.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: The move looks better than it did on Saturday. The pattern doesn't: every one of the previous three tight-end adds closed WRONG or CHURN in the log. One good night wouldn't change that; it would only mean the seat can finally be left alone.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Waller under five targets tonight with Coker out: then the role was never his, and Andrews (free, 10.1) is Tuesday's comparison. Leave it alone until then.

whatWentWrong.sources: NBC Sports · RotoWire · SI · ESPN · Week 1–3 archive

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: The tight-end comparison: free, healthy and now exactly level with Waller at 10.1. Hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Andrews 10.1 at home to Tennessee, Waller 10.1 against Detroit. Andrews runs a route on 65.6% of dropbacks with 23.7% of Baltimore's targets and is TE20 in points per game with no touchdown (FantasyPros, 4 Oct); 6, 7, 5 targets (archive). Zay Flowers is expected to play (Rapoport via NFL.com).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Level is a coin flip, and the seat changed hands on Saturday. Overnight the one risk to Waller's role, Coker playing, got less likely; and Tennessee are called the best defence against tight ends, though untested (FantasyPros).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing before Andrews' 11:00 kickoff: Carolina's inactives come at 16:50. Tuesday's question is whether Waller drew five targets.

case.label: What would change it

settled.title: Tuten for Lamar, the standing trade (19 Sep)
settled.result: Its own falsifier fired: Lamar is on Baltimore's Wednesday report, limited with a back issue (BaltimoreRavens.com 30 Sep). Never sent, no points lost. Closed WRONG, not held on a technicality.

settled.title: Add Pineiro, drop Loveland (25 Sep)
settled.result: Pineiro 6 to Little's 4 in Week 3 (archive), so the kicker half held, but the owner replaced him with Myers on Wednesday, five days after adding him. Closed CHURN.

settled.title: Add Gadsden as the second TE (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 0.0 on 3 targets in Week 3; dropped Wednesday for Sadiq. Closed WRONG. The written falsifier never fired, so it was badly written.

settled.title: Don't re-claim Hockenson (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Hockenson 3.1, Gadsden 0.0 in Week 3. Closed WRONG on the outcome, though the priority it saved was later spent anyway.

settled.title: Hold MarShawn Lloyd as Green Bay's lead back (19 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 4 carries, RB3 on snaps. Closed WRONG. Dropped Wednesday.

settled.title: Treat Rashee Rice as a sell-high (22 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 9 targets, 43% share, 15.8 points. Closed WRONG.

settled.title: Decline Rashod Bateman while Flowers plays (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Bateman 5.7 on 3 targets. Closed RIGHT.

settled.title: Don't claim Tate; take him if he clears (23 Sep)
settled.result: Added free, priority kept at 6th; scored his 11.8 projection exactly.

cannotSee.body: wire_screen.py counts Week 4 as a stat week once one game is played, so its list is Steelers and Browns plus Wicks and Higbee. Both passes returned the same eleven names as Saturday, so the verdicts are carried. It can't see Holani or Malik Washington; they're in do-not-chase from the ownership column.
